newsitem.title: USA: Calif. governor signs port safety agreements.
newsitem.headline: Calif. governor signs port safety agreements.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson said on Wednesday he signed agreements that would boost safety for ships using ports and harbors in the state and protect the coastal environment.

Wilson, a Republican, said the agreements would improve coordination between the state and the U.S. Coast Guard in monitoring ships, and enhance pilot training standards for tankers carrying oil and other potentially hazardous materials.

"This means, quite simply, that we've established a closer coordination between state and federal officials," Wilson said. "Our efforts to prevent or respond to oil spills no longer will be hindered by differing sets of regulations."
By signing the agreements, Wilson said California became the first state to implement the findings of the National Academy of Sciences' Marine Board.
It recommended that coastal states and states served by marine pilots create new or enhanced piloting programs in order to increase waterway safety and reduce the risk of collision or grounding.
